item.title: Version 1.11.1
item.description: **Fixes** - **The microphone is released when Settings closes.** The input level meter under Settings › Dictation › Microphone and Meetings › Recording kept the microphone open after the Settings window was closed, so macOS showed it as in use while nothing was being recorded. The meter now runs only while its window is visible, and stops when the window is closed, minimized or covered.

item.title: Version 1.11.0
item.description:
**Dictation** - **Choose the microphone.** Settings › Dictation has a new **Microphone** section and Settings › Meetings › Recording a **Meeting microphone** picker: the system default or a specific input device, each with a live input level meter while the pane is open, so dictation and meetings can use different microphones (also offered in setup's microphone step). Recording now uses an AVAudioEngine recorder that writes the same 16 kHz WAV as before, so live text and live meeting notes work unchanged. If the chosen microphone is not connected, Hlas records with the system default and says so in the popover. If the microphone disappears or changes format mid-dictation, the take stops with "Microphone changed; try again" instead of transcribing a cut-off recording, and the next take uses the default; in a meeting the microphone track stops there and the meeting continues. The previous recorder stays available for one release as a hidden setting (`defaults write com.hlas.app useLegacyRecorder -bool YES`, then a switch in Advanced). - **Live text while recording.** Settings › Dictation › Feedback has **Show live text while recording** (off by default; needs the on-screen indicator). With Parakeet or Bark loaded, the indicator pill shows the last two lines of what you are saying while you speak (the orb widens into a pill for it), and the popover's recording view shows the whole running text. Hlas re-transcribes the last 45 seconds about once a second, skips seconds that are silent, and applies your text rules to what it shows. The final text is still transcribed from the complete recording when you stop, so results are unchanged; stopping waits for a pass that is already running. Whisper is not supported (too slow per pass), and Speech models lists the feature under each engine. - **AI cleanup for other languages via your server.** Settings › Text output › Cleanup has a new **Other languages** group: **Clean up other languages with my meeting-notes server** (off by default) sends Czech, German or any other non-English dictation to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint set up under Meetings › Notes, with the same cleanup contract as S1-mini (fillers, self-corrections, punctuation, tone, bullet lists, email layout) and a reply in the dictation's language. **Also use it for English instead of S1-mini** sends English there too. Requests use temperature 0 and a 20-second limit; any failure (no server, HTTP error, timeout, implausible reply) keeps the text as dictated. Redaction from Meetings › Notes › Privacy applies. The language is that of the final text, so a dictation translated into Czech goes to the server. **Polish as…** on the last take follows the same rule. The on-screen indicator now reads "Cleaning up text", and the popover's text-output info mentions server cleanup when it is on. The toggles stay disabled until a notes base URL and model are saved. - **Spoken commands and snippets** in **Settings > Text output > Dictionary**. Turn on **Spoken commands** (off by default, dictation only) and say "comma", "period", "question mark", "exclamation mark", "colon", "semicolon", "new line", "new paragraph", "open quote" / "close quote", "open parenthesis" / "close parenthesis", "dash" or "scratch that" (deletes the last sentence of the take) to get the punctuation or line break instead of the word; Czech has "čárka", "tečka", "otazník", "vykřičník", "dvojtečka", "středník", "nový řádek", "nový odstavec", "pomlčka" and "škrtni to". The phrase list for your language is shown in Settings, and presets can switch the commands on or off. **Snippets** map a trigger phrase ("insert signature") to a multi-line text that is typed in verbatim, untouched by filler removal, smart punctuation and the dictionary; a snippet beats a dictionary entry with the same words. Smart punctuation now keeps line breaks and capitalizes the first word of each line. - The right-click menu has quick switches after **Recording Mode**: **Language** (your three most recent languages, Auto-detect and **Other…**, which opens the language setting; Parakeet shows "detected automatically", Bark "English only", and your own server hides it), a **Translate to <language>** checkbox, an **AI cleanup** checkbox, and **Paste Recent**, a submenu of your last five dictations that pastes the one you pick into the app you right-clicked from. Paste Recent is hidden when history saving is off. - The popover's last dictation has a new **More** menu (the ⋯ button on the transcript card): **Transcribe again with…** another engine whose model is downloaded (or your own server), **Polish as…** Casual, Semi-casual, Semi-formal, Formal or plain text, **Translate to…** one of your three most recent target languages (macOS 15+), and **Edit…**, which turns the card into a text area with **Save & Paste** (⌘↩), **Save** and **Cancel** (Esc). Right-click a word while editing and choose **Add to dictionary…** to teach Hlas the right spelling; saving turns the personal dictionary on if it was off. Every change updates the same History record instead of adding a new one, and History can now edit dictation records too. To make this possible Hlas keeps the last recording in memory (never on disk) for 10 minutes or until the next dictation; turn **Keep the last recording so you can retry it** off in **Settings > Privacy & permissions** to drop it right away. Takes longer than 5 minutes keep their text only. - New **Insert text by** option in **Settings > Dictation**: **Pasting** (default, as before) or **Typing keystrokes**. Typing sends the text key by key instead of pressing Cmd-V, so it works where pasting is blocked (terminals, remote desktops, password fields, some Electron inputs) and never touches your clipboard. It is slower for long text. If you switch to another app while Hlas is typing, it stops and leaves the full transcript on the clipboard. - New **Give Whisper these words as hints** option in **Settings > Text output > Dictionary** (off by default). With the personal dictionary on, Whisper is shown your dictionary's replacement words before transcribing, so names such as "Hlas" are spelled right instead of being corrected afterwards. Whisper only; Parakeet and Bark cannot take hints and still rely on the dictionary replacements. Each hinted take costs one extra short decoder pass.
**Presets and triggers** - Dictation presets. **Settings > Dictation > Presets** lets you save named sets of changes for one dictation: recording mode, language (Whisper only), translation, AI cleanup with its tone, bullet lists and email layout, filler-word removal, smart punctuation, the personal dictionary, paste automatically, press Return after pasting and **Insert text by**. Each setting is **Default** (your global setting) or a fixed value. Give a preset its own shortcut, and it appears under **Preset shortcuts** in the popover; the popover reads "Listening · <preset>" while it records. The new **Apps** section applies a preset automatically when you dictate into a chosen app, and a preset's own shortcut still wins over the app's preset, setting by setting. Retrying the last take repeats the settings it was dictated with. Deleting a preset removes its shortcut and its app rules, and a shortcut that is already taken by the recording shortcut, the meeting shortcut or another preset is refused. - The **Fn / Globe key** and a **mouse button** can start dictation too. Under the shortcut in **Settings > Dictation**, turn on **Fn / Globe key** and/or record a mouse button (click **Click to record…**, then press a side button; left, right and middle click are refused). Both follow the recording mode: hold and release, or press to start and press again to finish. Fn combinations such as Fn+F5 or Fn+arrow keep working and never start a dictation. The chosen mouse button no longer reaches other apps, so a browser doesn't also go Back; other buttons are untouched. If macOS uses the Globe key for Emoji & Symbols or Dictation, the pane says so and opens Keyboard Settings, and a permission row appears if Accessibility or Input Monitoring is missing. While one of them records, the popover and the indicator say "Release the key or button" instead of naming the shortcut.
**Meetings** - Meetings can be paused. While a meeting records, the pause button next to **Finish meeting** in the popover, **Pause** in the meeting window and **Pause Meeting Recording** in the right-click menu stop both the microphone and Mac audio together; **Resume** picks up again and **Stop & transcribe** finishes from the paused state. The skipped stretch is left out of both tracks, so the transcript has no gap and speaker labels stay aligned. Every meeting timer now shows recorded time only, and the menu bar icon shows a pause symbol while paused. The meeting shortcut still starts and stops. - Meeting transcripts can show when each turn started. Turn on **Show timestamps** in **Settings > Meetings > Recording** (off by default) to get `[12:34] Speaker 1: …`. It works without speaker labels too: the transcript is then split into paragraphs at pauses, which now also happens with timestamps off. History and the meeting window can export a meeting as SubRip (`.srt`) or WebVTT (`.vtt`) subtitles as well as plain text and Markdown (new **Export transcript…** button in the meeting window). Hlas now asks the speech engine for word timings on every meeting, so Whisper meetings take longer. - **Rename speakers.** Click a speaker's label ("Speaker 2:") in the meeting window's Transcript tab or in History, type a name such as "Petra" and press Save; Reset brings back "Me" or "Speaker N". All of that speaker's turns change together, and so do the saved transcript (re-rendered with the current timestamp setting, so History's row preview follows), the meeting notes (action owners, note text and the quoted source excerpts) and the History record. Notes still being written when you rename are updated when they arrive. Names apply to that meeting only, and a name another speaker already has is refused.
**Files** - **Transcribe audio and video files.** Drop a file on the menu bar icon or into the open popover, or choose **Transcribe File…** in the right-click menu. WAV, AIFF, CAF, M4A, MP3, FLAC, MOV, MP4 and M4V files up to 3 hours are decoded and transcribed on your Mac with the selected local engine, exactly like a recorded meeting: speaker labels (without "Me"), timestamps, subtitle export and meeting notes all apply. The meeting window shows **Preparing audio…** with a progress bar while the file is decoded. The result is saved to History with a **File** badge and the file name as its title; History's filter gains **File**, and **Export…** suggests the file name. The file is only read, never changed or deleted. A file is refused while a meeting records or is being transcribed, or while you dictate, and the popover says why; if transcription fails, **Retry** decodes the file again. Both channels of a stereo file are kept, so an interview recorded with one voice per channel loses neither.
**Meeting notes and questions** - **Ask the meeting a question.** A new **Ask** tab in the meeting window, and in History for meetings and transcribed files: type a question and press **Ask** (⌘↩). The answer comes from the transcript only, with the excerpts that support it under **Source excerpts**; a question the transcript answers only partly is marked **Partly answered**, and one it does not answer gets **Not in the transcript**. Long transcripts are answered section by section, then combined. Uses the meeting notes endpoint (the question and the transcript are sent to it when you ask); without one the tab offers **Configure meeting notes…**. Questions and answers are saved with the History record (newest 50) and History search finds them. The meeting notes request code now shares its HTTP transport with this feature; notes requests are unchanged.
**Privacy** - **Redact personal data before it leaves the Mac.** Settings › Meetings › Notes has a new **Privacy** section: **Replace names, emails and phone numbers before sending** (off by default) and a list of extra terms such as company or project names. When it is on, live drafts, final notes and questions reach the notes endpoint with placeholders ("Person A", "Term A", `email-1@example.invalid`, `+000 000 001`), the same throughout a meeting; dates and amounts are kept, and so are "Me" and "Speaker N", while a name you gave a speaker is replaced. Notes and answers show the original names again, and source excerpts always come from the original transcript. **Preview redaction…** shows the current or latest meeting transcript as the endpoint would see it. Best effort: names are found with Apple's Natural Language framework (strongest in English), emails and phone numbers by pattern. The debug log only records how many values were replaced.
**Automation** - **Automation: Shortcuts actions and `hlas://` URLs.** The Shortcuts app lists Hlas actions: Start, Stop (returns the transcript), Toggle and Cancel Dictation, Dictate with Preset, Toggle / Pause / Resume Meeting Recording, Transcribe Audio File (file in, text out) and Get Last Transcript; Spotlight and Siri know "Start dictation in Hlas" and similar phrases. Raycast, Stream Deck, Keyboard Maestro and scripts can open `hlas://dictation/start|stop|toggle|cancel`, `hlas://dictation/start?preset=<name>`, `hlas://meeting/toggle|pause|resume`, `hlas://transcribe?file=<path>`, `hlas://paste-last` and `hlas://settings/<section>`; Settings › App › **Automation** lists them with Copy buttons. URL commands are off by default: turn them on with **Allow hlas:// URL commands** in Settings › App › Automation. Any app or web page that opens a hlas:// link could otherwise start or stop dictation and paste text; while the switch is off, Hlas ignores every hlas:// URL. Shortcuts actions are not affected by the switch and always work. Both run the same checks as the popover, refuse with a reason while Hlas is busy, and do nothing until setup is complete. `transcribe` only reads audio or video files in your home folder or under `/Volumes`.
**Fixes** - Auto-detect with Whisper now actually detects the language. Until now Hlas never asked Whisper to detect it, so Auto-detect quietly behaved like English and returned wrong text for other languages. Choosing a specific language is unchanged. - Meeting recordings now mix both stereo channels of system audio into the transcript track. Before, only the left channel was kept, so a voice a conference app panned to the right could be missing. - Recorded audio read back from disk (dictation takes, the meeting microphone track, a retried meeting) is now read to the end; a single read could stop a few hundredths of a second short.

item.title: Version 1.10.1
item.description: - Setup now offers Bark as a speech model. Open **Other speech models** in the speech-model step and choose **Bark · English only**, then pick Plus (about 200 MB) or Pro (about 1.2 GB). The download starts when you click Prepare. - If the language you chose earlier in setup is not English, setup warns that Bark only understands English and offers **Set language to English**. - On macOS 14, setup explains that Bark requires macOS 15.

item.title: Version 1.10.0
item.description:
**Bark 3.0 speech recognition** - Added Bark 3.0 (Underdog Bark, by Conway Research) as a local speech engine in **Settings > Speech models**, next to Parakeet and Whisper. It runs entirely on this Mac and needs macOS 15 or later; on macOS 14 it is shown as unavailable. - Bark understands English only. Other languages come out as wrong text rather than an error, so Hlas warns when your language is not English and offers a one-click "Set language to English". - Two versions: Bark 3.0 Plus (about 200 MB, the default) and Bark 3.0 Pro (about 1.2 GB, most accurate). The pane shows each version's published English word error rate (4.76% and 4.29%). These are the model authors' benchmark figures, not measurements from Hlas. - The first load prepares the model for your Mac and can take a few minutes. Bark writes every word, including "um" and "uh"; turn on Remove filler words or AI cleanup in **Settings > Text output** to drop them. - Works with AI cleanup, translation out of English, meetings, and meeting speaker labels. Audio never leaves this Mac.
**Know each engine's limits** - **Settings > Speech models** now lists what each engine supports and where it falls short (languages, translation, size, meetings, speed), including for Own server. The Language section explains how language selection works for the engine you chose.
**Downloaded model storage** - Added a Downloaded models section in **Settings > Speech models** that lists every Parakeet, Whisper, and Bark model on disk with its size and a total. Download a Parakeet or Whisper model without switching to it, or delete any you no longer use. - The model currently in use is marked and cannot be deleted; switch engines first. A leftover Parakeet cache from an earlier version appears here too, so you can reclaim its space.
**Other** - Updated the speech runtime (FluidAudio) to 0.17.7. The Parakeet model location is unchanged, so there is no re-download.

item.title: Version 1.9.1
item.description: - Added a live memory meter in **Settings > Speech models**, with Hlas's total memory use, a recent-usage graph, and estimates for loaded speech, cleanup, and speaker-label models. The meter updates once a second while the pane is open. - Model estimates follow loading, first use, switching, and unloading. When a model's memory cannot be separated from the rest of Hlas, it shows **No estimate**; the total still includes it. Search settings for "memory" to find the meter. - Fixed a cleanup-model loading race when cleanup is turned off and immediately enabled again, preventing a canceled load from overwriting the current state. - Marked Parakeet as the recommended speech engine for supported languages in Settings and setup.

item.title: Version 1.9.0
item.description:
**Live meeting notes** - Added a meeting window with Notes and Transcript tabs. With notes enabled, drafts refresh about every 30 seconds when the speech engine is available; finishing the meeting generates notes from the complete final transcript. - Choose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and model in **Settings > Meetings > Notes**. Local servers such as LM Studio and compatible external providers are supported, with model discovery, an optional Keychain API key, and provider compatibility options. - Notes organize summaries, decisions, actions, and open questions, with original source excerpts for review. Copy or export Markdown from the meeting window or History. - Notes are optional and off by default. Meeting audio is transcribed on your Mac; enabling notes sends transcript text to the endpoint you choose. Review generated notes against the transcript before using them as minutes. - Failed notes requests preserve the transcript and last successful draft. Final notes are saved with the meeting when History saving is enabled.
**Focused settings** - Split Text output into Cleanup, Dictionary, and Translation sections, and Meetings into Recording, Notes, and Reminders. - Each category remembers its last section. Search opens the matching section, including advanced notes-provider controls.

item.title: Version 1.8.3
item.description: - Automatic update checks are on by default and can be turned off in Settings > App. Hlas checks at startup and every hour while running, respecting your saved preference. - Failed automatic checks stay silent, including startup configuration failures. Manual checks remain available when automatic checking is off. - Available update alerts now have a menu-bar indicator and a versioned right-click menu item, making background alerts easier to find.

item.title: Version 1.8.2
item.description: - Added **Follow focused display** in Settings > Dictation > Feedback, enabled by default. The on-screen indicator follows the active window's display while visible, carrying its dragged position across displays. If window focus is unavailable, it uses the pointer's display. Turn the setting off to keep the indicator at its saved position. - Recording failure messages now disappear after three seconds instead of ten, followed by the existing short fade.

item.title: Version 1.8.1
item.description:
**A clearer everyday interface** - Redesigned the menu around a prominent Dictate button, a separate meeting action, clearer recording status, and labeled recording and text-output controls. - Added a last-transcript card with completion time, expansion, copy and paste actions. - Made Settings more compact, with grouped navigation, search and clearer descriptions. Processing location now distinguishes This Mac from Own server. - Made the local S1-mini polishing model and its English-only dictation support more visible.
**Guided setup** - Added a five-step setup window with saved progress, an animated explanation of the dictation flow, model preparation, optional automatic paste, and real practice dictation. - Manual copy and paste remains available without Accessibility access. Practice does not paste text, save history, translate, or apply AI cleanup.
**Feedback and recovery** - Refined the recording orb and readable indicator, including the Settings preview. - Clarified clipboard fallback, paste requests, translation failures and history-save outcomes. If translation fails, the original text is kept and English polishing is skipped. - Improved History with an adaptive list/detail layout, Undo Delete and clearer deletion confirmation. - Added a meeting status window with input activity and a visible, cancelable auto-start countdown. - Improved keyboard accessibility and support for reduced motion.

item.title: Version 1.8.0
item.description:
**Meeting speaker labels** - Optionally identify speakers in meeting transcripts with an on-device model. Enable "Identify speakers" in Settings > Meetings and download the model (~200 MB). Speaker identification runs locally after transcription. - Speakers are numbered in order of appearance. When microphone and system-audio activity clearly distinguish your voice, your turns are labeled "Me". - If speaker identification or word alignment fails, Hlas keeps the complete plain transcript. Failed meeting transcriptions can still be retried from the saved audio. - Model downloads, deletion, and transcription are coordinated to prevent overlapping model operations.
**Local Parakeet** - Updated the local speech engine. Existing Parakeet users need a one-time model download (~470 MB) because the model files and cache location have changed.
**Whisper model loading** - Reuse an already downloaded model without checking the old Documents cache, avoiding an unnecessary Documents permission prompt during loading.

item.title: Version 1.7.2
item.description: - New Fast | Polished switch in the menu bar popover toggles AI cleanup (S1-mini) without opening Settings. Fast gives the raw transcript with no post-processing delay.

item.title: Version 1.7.0
item.description: **On-screen indicator** - The floating recording indicator is now a small translucent orb instead of a wide pill — it shows your input level while recording, a spinner while transcribing, and a checkmark when the text lands. - **Drag it anywhere.** Where you leave it is where it comes back, on whichever screen you put it. "Reset indicator position" in Settings › General puts it back at the bottom of the screen. - The transcript itself no longer appears in the indicator — it goes where you're typing, which is where you were already looking. Errors still show their message in full.

item.title: Version 1.6.1
item.description: **Updates** - Hlas now checks for new versions on its own and offers the update when it finds one. Previously it only asked for permission to check on first launch, and did nothing at all if that prompt was declined or dismissed — so updates could be missed indefinitely unless you picked "Check for Updates…" from the menu-bar menu by hand. - This fix only takes effect from this version onward: it is the 1.6.1 binary that knows to check, so 1.6.1 is the last update you may need to reach for the menu item to get.

item.title: Version 1.6.0
item.description:
**Text** - **AI cleanup** (Settings › Text, off by default) — rewrites the transcript on-device with **"S1-mini" by "Superwhisper"**: fillers removed, self-corrections resolved to what you landed on, punctuation and capitalization applied, and spoken numbers, dates, currency and email addresses written out. Four tones, optional bullet lists, optional email layout. English only; downloads a ~350 MB model on first use and runs entirely on your Mac. - Filler-word removal and smart punctuation are disabled while AI cleanup is on — the model does both jobs, and running them together mangles its output. The personal dictionary still applies, before the model sees the text.
**Build** - Xcode 26 and the separately-downloadable Metal toolchain (`xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain`) are now required.

item.title: Version 1.5.0
item.description:
**Dictation** - Optional floating on-screen indicator while recording/transcribing, with error feedback (Settings › General › Feedback; off by default) - Press Esc to cancel a recording; Cancel button in the popover - Optional sound cues (off by default); Launch at Login - "Paste again" and tap-to-expand for the last transcript; Copy/Paste Last Transcription and Recording Mode in the menu-bar right-click menu - Too-quiet takes now say so instead of silently doing nothing; errors are shown on the menu-bar icon
**Settings & History** - Settings reorganised into General, Transcription, Translation, Text, Meetings, Advanced; window keeps its size and position - Whisper models show downloaded state and size, can be deleted or re-downloaded - History: select, delete (Delete key / context menu), group by day, filter dictation vs meeting, Clear History; "Save transcripts to History" toggle and retention period - Personal dictionary is an editable table - Onboarding lets you choose Parakeet or Whisper and shows download progress
**Fixes & privacy** - Microphone recovers after sleep/wake (wake listener never fired before) - Translation can no longer hang the app - Dictionary replacements containing `$` or `\` no longer corrupt text; filler-word removal no longer deletes "like"/"actually" - Dictation audio is deleted from disk after transcription; transcripts no longer written to the debug log or notifications - Clipboard is restored faithfully (images, rich text), transcripts are hidden from clipboard managers, and paste/Enter only fire in the app you dictated from - Meeting audio is kept until transcription succeeds, with a Retry button - Remote server: no default address, unencrypted-connection warning, more reliable transfer and clearer errors
